from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Projective Intuition", [
            "The dot product measures projection.",
            "Vector A casts a shadow on vector B.",
            "This shadow length signifies the projection."
        ])
        
        # Load Assets
        sun = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sun.svg")
        flashlight = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/flashlight.svg")
        
        # Create visual elements
        # Vector B: Origin to RIGHT
        origin_pt = self.grid['E2']
        vec_b = Arrow(origin_pt, origin_pt + RIGHT * 3, color=BLUE, buff=0)
        vec_a = Arrow(origin_pt, origin_pt + UP * 2 + RIGHT * 1, color=RED, buff=0)
        
        # Projection: perpendicular from tip of A to B
        projection_end = origin_pt + RIGHT * 1
        projection_line = DashedLine(vec_a.get_end(), projection_end, color=WHITE)
        projection_shadow = Line(origin_pt, projection_end, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=8)
        
        label_p = MathTex("p", color=YELLOW)
        point_A = Dot(vec_a.get_end(), color=RED)
        
        # Apply positioning constraints
        self.place_at_grid(sun, 'A5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(projection_shadow, 'D2', 'F4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(label_p, 'E4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(point_A, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(sun), Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b), FadeIn(point_A))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(Create(projection_line), FadeIn(flashlight))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(projection_shadow), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(sun, flashlight, vec_a, vec_b, projection_line, projection_shadow, label_p, point_A)))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Dot Product as a Linear Map", ["Dot product is a linear map.", "It returns a scalar from two vectors.", "A fixed vector w defines this function."])
        
        # Elements
        w_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg", color="#FF0000")
        matrix_m = MathTex(r"M = \begin{bmatrix} w_1 & w_2 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        vector_v = MathTex(r"v = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}", color="#FF0000")
        result = MathTex(r"f(v) = w \cdot v = x \cdot w_1 + y \cdot w_2", color="#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.place_at_grid(w_icon, "A3", scale_factor=0.5)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Duality connects vectors to linear functionals.",
            "The dot product acts as a bridge.",
            "Every functional corresponds to a vector.",
            "Vectors act as measuring devices.",
            "Duality merges object and operation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Duality", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg", color=RED)
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg", color="#FF00FF")
        
        v_space = Circle(radius=0.4, color=BLUE).add(Text("V", font_size=16, color=BLUE))
        scalar_space = Circle(radius=0.4, color=RED).add(Text("R", font_size=16, color=RED))
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.5, end=RIGHT*0.5, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        dual_label = Text("Dual Space", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dual_label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'C1', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Write(dual_label), FadeIn(compass))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(v_space, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(scalar_space, 'D5')
        self.place_in_area(arrow, 'D3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(v_space), Create(scalar_space), GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        dot_product_label = MathTex(r"f(v) = w \cdot v", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_product_label, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(dot_product_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        sensor_box = Square(side_length=0.4, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(sensor_box, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(sensor_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, 'F4', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Indicate(v_space), Indicate(scalar_space), FadeIn(ruler))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Duality via Level Sets", [
            "Dot product defines perpendicular level sets.", 
            "Vector w sets plane orientation.", 
            "Level sets map the dual space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Vectors are points, duals are tools.",
            "Dot product bridges geometry and functions.",
            "It translates operations into states."
        ])
        
        # Visual objects
        point = Dot(color=BLUE)
        point_label = Text("Point", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        
        tool = VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.3), Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*0.3)).set_color(GREEN)
        tool_label = Text("Dual Tool", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(point, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(point_label, 'C1', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(tool, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(tool_label, 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(point, point_label, tool, tool_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        bridge = Arrow(self.grid['C2'], self.grid['C5'], color=RED)
        self.add(bridge)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        state_label_group = Text("Operational State", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(state_label_group, 'E3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.add(state_label_group)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Dot Products and the Concept of Duality

sections.title: Prerequisite: Projective Intuition
sections.content: Briefly establish the geometric meaning of a dot product: the projection of one vector onto another. Visualize a light source casting a shadow of vector A onto vector B.
sections.example: A flashlight shining on a stick (vector A) resting on the ground (vector B), creating a shadow length.

sections.title: Defining the Dot Product as a Linear Map
sections.content: Shift the perspective from 'multiplying two vectors' to 'a function that takes a vector and returns a scalar'. Introduce the dot product with a fixed vector 'w' as a linear transformation f(v) = w · v.
sections.example: A sensor (vector w) sweeping across a field; the dot product tells us the 'intensity' of data detected at any point v.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Duality
sections.content: Explain duality: Every vector space has an associated dual space of linear functionals. The dot product acts as the bridge, showing that every 'operation' (linear functional) can be represented by a 'state' (a vector).
sections.example: A robot (vector w) is defined by its sensing capabilities. The dual perspective treats the robot not as an object, but as a 'detector' that evaluates its environment.

sections.title: Visualizing Duality via Level Sets
sections.content: Show that the dot product w · v = c represents a plane (or line) perpendicular to w. The 'vector' w determines the orientation of these planes—this is the geometric essence of the dual space.
sections.example: Imagine a flock of birds flying. The 'dual vector' represents the direction of the wind force; the level sets are the imaginary boundaries where the wind pressure is constant.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Vectors are points; dual vectors are 'measuring devices'. The dot product is the bridge that allows us to translate between geometry and function.
sections.example: In computer graphics: A surface normal (vector) and the lighting function (dual) interact via the dot product to determine shading intensity on a character's face.
